claims.statement: Two Z4 characters recover the composition of shortest nontrivial holonomy cycles.
claims.evidence: Analytic closed-walk decomposition; exact fixed benchmark.

claims.statement: 1,389 assignments agree with independent cycle enumeration.
claims.evidence: Fixed screen and validation result JSON.
claims.limitation: Nine small graph families; girth baseline also succeeds.

claims.statement: Shortest nontrivial loop length equals shortest path from a vertex to a different sheet of its Z4 lift, minimized over vertices.
claims.limitation: Finite simple graphs, discrete phases; not a physical theory.

claims.statement: All 356 assignments pass three independent calculations and exact trace inversion.
claims.evidence: 43 connected labeled graphs and four fixed cactus graphs.
claims.limitation: Small fixed domains; not a performance or novelty claim.

claims.statement: Ordinary girth determines the shortest nontrivial holonomy loop given nonflatness.
claims.evidence: 21 counterexamples in the follow-up; triangle-square bridge witness.
claims.limitation: Refutes the universal assertion, not usefulness on particular families.

claims.statement: First faithful deficit and its order determine both shortest-cycle flux counts.
claims.evidence: 440 unordered within-graph collision pairs; two-triangle witness.
claims.limitation: Only the first scalar deficit, not entire faithful spectrum, is refuted.

claims.statement: Discrete loop holonomy may model physically measurable distributed information.
